invariants: The SQL API owner creates the control and fixed pthread pool as sibling Workers. Before loading the module, the control installs MessagePort Worker facades that preserve SDK onmessage/onerror properties and transfer lists; the API owner bounds allocations and terminates the entire group on every retirement path.

Normal native exit completes cleanup and clears pthread_self before publishing DT_EXITED. After native joins and SDK pool return drain all pthread mappings, normal close terminates the idle pool without a second child acknowledgement; browser target gates independently verify physical reclamation.
The checkMailbox postset preserves SDK dispatch while live and gates queued callbacks before a fatal module or storage owner terminates native lock owners.

A failed pthread handles a private cmd-less retirement message on its own JS event loop, acknowledges through a MessagePort and closes its scope without native cleanup; its parent excludes it from terminateAllThreads and waits for that acknowledgement.
A clear waiting_async flag selects SDK postMessage mailbox delivery, including pthread cancellation and reuse.
ProxyingQueue.queue identifies the public C queue executed by emscripten_proxy_execute_queue on its target thread.
Async proxy submission publishes work before notifying; duplicate notifications can observe an empty queue.
The SQL control Worker stays live until replies are delivered; the I/O owner drains independently through its direct channel.
PThread.pthreads maps pthread identities to Worker objects; terminateAllThreads skips an explicitly removed I/O owner and does not free terminated thread data.
The pthread message handler ignores messages without a cmd field, allowing a private MessagePort to close OPFS handles without entering a failed Wasm module.
MAIN_THREAD_EM_ASM synchronously dispatches to the SQL control Worker; owner registration completes before the I/O thread publishes readiness.
For the pinned wasm32 layout pthread is 120 bytes and its final 4-byte atomic member is wait_addr; failure snapshots read it only for live entries owned by the control Worker.
